examples.scenario: Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) affiliate deploys a multi-stage ransomware payload via malicious PowerShell downloader on corporate endpoints, leveraging living-off-the-land binaries and obfuscated scripts to evade detection. The ransomware encrypts files and drops ransom notes while communicating with C2 servers for encryption key exchange.

indicators: Domain malicious.example.com used in payload download
Registry persistence under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run with suspicious PowerShell command
Process chain powershell.exe -> rundll32.exe loading payload.dll
examples.detection_method: Monitor for anomalous PowerShell command-line arguments with web client download and rundll32 execution; Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) alert on creation of rundll32.exe loading unsigned DLL from temp folder; Network IDS/IPS detecting HTTP GET for known malicious payload URLs; DNS logs for suspicious domain resolutions; Monitor registry Run keys for unexpected entries; Analyze outbound connections for unusual HTTPS POSTs to rare or new domains; Detect processes accessing multiple user file extensions rapidly.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1566.001 - Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment (initial access vector via phishing links to payload)
T1059.001 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1547.001 - Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
